subject: Acme Retail — Night peak SSE tail latency / p95-p99 spike
messages:

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 02:47:00 -0000
Subject: Realtime chat slowness during night promo — 02:30-03:15 UTC

Hi team,

We started seeing severe slowdowns on the embedded chat during our night promo window (02:30–03:15 UTC). The UI shows messages delayed by several seconds and a fraction of sessions disconnecting. Our telemetry shows 95th/99th percentile response times for streaming messages jumped by ~4–8x.

This is impacting checkout helpers on mobile, causing abandoned flows. I’ve attached a small sample of client-side traces and server logs. Can someone confirm if there were any config or capacity changes on your side?

Attachments: logs_tail_20281005.txt (excerpt), client_traces.json (excerpt)

Thanks,
Elena
Senior Engineering Manager — Customer Ops
Acme Retail

Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 03:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime chat slowness during night promo — 02:30-03:15 UTC

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m looping in Aditya (AM) and Marcus (SRE on call). We’ll triage immediately and get you an ETA.

Current ask: Marcus, can you validate whether the streaming SSE pool serving acme-retail-app-prod had any autoscaler activity or node OOMs during the 02:20–03:30 UTC window? Also please check if prefix caching behaved differently for short-turn dialogues.

—Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 03:15:30 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime chat slowness during night promo — triage notes

Triage notes (initial):
- Checked metrics for cluster acme-prod-sse-us-east. Autoscaler did trigger 1 scale event at 02:40 UTC but scaled slowly due to spot reclamation.
- No OOM logs on primary G4 nodes but increased context-switch CPU during peak; NVMe I/O remained normal.
- Observed increased KV-cache miss ratio for conversation prefixes for tenant acme-retail-app-prod — miss rate jumped 12% -> 48% at the beginning of the window.
- p95 and p99 for message-append latency (SSE) moved from ~80ms/220ms baseline to ~350ms/1.8s during 02:35–02:55 UTC.

Immediate mitigation performed at 03:05 UTC: pinned a hot-path model variant (quantized fallback) for ACME routing and bumped reserved pool capacity. Latency improved but tail remains elevated for long conversations.

Next steps: collect a wider trace window (02:15–03:30), share Humio query link, and coordinate rollback or permanent quota bump if this repeats during next night promo.

—Marcus
SRE — Serving Runtime
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Elena Morgan <elena.morgan@acme-retail.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 03:24:10 -0000
Subject: Re: Realtime chat slowness during night promo — interim update

Elena — thanks for reporting and for the traces. Marcus shared the initial triage below. We pushed a quick mitigation (reserve hot capacity + route to a quantized compatible variant) at 03:05 UTC which brought p95 down to ~140ms and p99 to ~420ms for new sessions, but long-running sessions that hit higher sequence lengths are still suffering.

I want to be transparent: this appears to be a combined pressure point — KV cache churn from ephemeral short-turn conversations during the promo + slower autoscaler ramp because a portion of the fleet was spot-backed and reclaimed. We are treating this as priority-high and putting an action item for: (1) temporary reserved buffer for your night-promo windows, (2) investigate per-tenant cache warming, (3) autoscaler tuning for spot reclamation scenarios.

Can you confirm whether you have any additional scheduled promos next week or variable concurrency we should pre-provision for? We’ll prepare a short runbook for the night window by EOD.

—Aditya
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morgan <elena.morgan@acme-retail.com>

Thanks Aditya — we do have two more night promos scheduled in October (10/12 and 10/26) with similar expected user concurrency (estimated +5–7x baseline). The 10/12 window is lower risk and can be used as a canary if you need it.

Ops team: please share any logs we missed. We appreciate the quick mitigation.

—Elena
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 06:20:00 -0000
Subject: Executive note + request for exec attention — Acme night promos

Team — brief executive summary for leadership/ops:
- Impact: ACME experienced elevated p95/p99 on streaming chat SSE during a promotional traffic spike overnight (peak 02:30–02:55 UTC). Topline customer impact was slow responses in checkout help; some sessions dropped.
- Root causes (initial): cache churn of short-turn conversations (high prefix miss), slower autoscaler ramp due to spot instance reclamation, and longer sequence lengths causing quantized model fallbacks to surface tail work.
- Actions taken: hot-path model pinning + reserved pool bump improved new-session latency; comprehensive trace exported.
- Ask for execs: temporary reserved capacity for Acme night windows (~+20% headroom for 10/12 and 10/26), and approval to prioritize an autoscaler resilience patch (spot-safe ramp + proactive warm nodes).

Attachments: humio-link.txt (trace queries), logs_tail_20281005.txt

I’ll coordinate a short post-mortem and a proposed commitment for guaranteed night window capacity. Please advise if we should loop in legal/finance for a temporary credits/discount conversation with ACME.

—Aditya
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
